newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam eyes nuclear energy to meet power needs.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam eyes nuclear energy to meet power needs.

text.p: Vietnam, facing pressure on its energy resources from a fast-growing economy, said on Thursday it was likely to need a nuclear power industry within 15 years.

Tran Viet Ngai, deputy director-general of the Vietnam Electricity Corporation, was quoted by official newspapers as saying that at current rates of increase the country's thermal and hydro-power resources would be unable to meet demand after 2010.
He said plans had been made for a nuclear power industry and suggested the first plant should be built in a remote unpopulated area of the country in order to minimise risks from a nuclear accident.
Vietnam's economy is currently growing at a rate of around 9.5 percent each year, with power output increasing about 15 percent annually.
The newspaper reports said output needed to increase by around double the rate of economic growth in order to meet demand.
Vietnam said last year it was studying plans for a $3 billion nuclear power plant, which if approved would begin operating within 20 years.
However some officials have opposed the idea on grounds of safety and concerns over the disposal of waste.
Vietnam currently has one nuclear reactor in the southern hill station of Dalat, which it says is used for experimental purposes only.
Hanoi is a signatory to the Nuclear Non-proliferation Treaty and was among more than 50 nations which signed a Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty earlier this week at the UN headquarters in New York.
